2018_128_121818regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of December 18, 2018 at the Services Building — the year's closing meeting and Todd Miletti's last after 12 years. The Board formally names the new preschool building the Troy School District Preschool, awards $5,313,940.00 of Bid Pack 23 work across five buildings, and finally settles the Early Childhood Center casework at $662,570.00 after two failed bid rounds. The November 13 minutes carried here record the aftermath of the November 6 election, at which voters approved a replacement non-homestead operating millage of 21 mills with 18 the maximum allowable levy, and the Board's amended L-4029 setting the levy at 18 mills.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, December 18, 2018, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois.

**Recognition**
The Mission Moment recognizes the group developing "a world-class foundation for a comprehensive pre-kindergarten education experience for our youngest learners" — Kris Griffor and Erin Keyser share a video of the Early Childhood Center.

The second item is **Todd Miletti's 12 years of service**, this being his final meeting. The write-up notes that aside from being an elected position, serving on the Board is also a volunteer position requiring a great deal of time, effort and commitment, and that Miletti "has done a remarkable service to past and future generations of Troy students."

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the November 13 special meeting, closed session and workshop, the November 20 meeting, and the October 2018 Treasurer's Report.

**The millage, after the vote**
The November 13 special meeting existed to true up the tax levy. The 2018-19 Budget Appropriations Resolution adopted June 19, 2018 had authorized **17.6840 mills** on non-homestead property. At the November 6, 2018 election the district's electors approved a replacement non-homestead operating millage of **21 mills, with 18 mills being the maximum allowable levy**, effective for the 2018 calendar year. Resolution 18-085 amends the appropriations resolution to authorize a levy of **18 mills**, and authorizes the President and Secretary to sign an amended 2018 Tax Rate Request (Form L-4029) with **9.158 of the 18 mills levied on the December 1, 2018 levy date**, for submission to the Oakland County Clerk. It carried 5-0 with Miletti and Philippart absent.

**Also from November**
The November 13 workshop covered the Troy High sign, the Consumers and DTE easements at Boulan Park, the Boyd Street property sale and sidewalk, and board professional learning on **school start times**; Judge Kirsten Hartig and Dr. Nicole Wilson were in the audience.

The November 20 minutes record 18-087 through 18-092, all 6-0 with Miletti absent: the consent agenda, Cornelissen's appointment, the Signarama sign award at $21,739.30, the Boyd Street sale to Delmar Homes at $10,000.00, and — added to the agenda at Mr. Gottlieb's request — **resolution 18-091 directing Dr. Machesky and Human Resources to develop a succession plan** to maintain continuity and consistency of the district into the future and share it with the Board. The Troy College & Career High School Mission Moment described a Trunk or Treat event, a book drive that collected and delivered **more than 2,000 books** for students in Pontiac Schools, and a partnership with Oakmont Senior Living where students help with iPads, call bingo and perform skits for residents who often have no family nearby.

**Treasurer's Report — October 2018**
Total check disbursements are $9,173,492.59, the General Fund group $4,711,884.58 and the General Fund (101) itself $4,479,154.93. With $2,045,278.46 of wire transfers, $267,995.65 of P-Card purchases and $29,426.83 of ACH debits, less an unusually large $369,076.31 of prior period void disbursements, total disbursements in period are $11,147,117.22.

**Business 8.A — the casework, third time**
The Early Childhood Center casework and millwork had failed to draw acceptable bids in March and again in September. On this third attempt RFP 9864 produced 5 bidders in each category — but the bids came in over the construction budget. Rob Carson's November 29 memo records that collaborative efforts between the bond construction team and the low bidders identified **options which created cost savings while maintaining intent and function of the original design**. The award is Mica-Tec interior architectural millwork at $442,920.00 — reduced from a $515,000.00 base bid by three options totalling deductions of $24,180.00, $41,314.00 and $6,586.00 — and Architect Systems Group prefabricated casework at $219,650.00, for **$662,570.00** from the Early Childhood Center Fund. Mica-Tec's base bid was already well below the next bidders at $574,121.00, $576,400.00, $615,810.00 and $714,000.00.

**Business 8.B — Bid Pack 23**
The largest single award of the year after the preschool itself. The scope covers mechanical/electrical upgrades and window/door replacements at Schroeder, Troy Union and Smith; the Smith kitchen renovation; kitchen equipment for Barnard, Bemis and Hamilton; renovation of the Troy High auto and wood shop classrooms; conversion of the closed swimming pool area into classrooms at International Academy East; and bathroom renovation plus a new office suite for the TCT program at the International Academy building.

Thirteen contracts total **$5,313,940.00**, split by funding source: **$2,979,173.00 from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund, $1,725,961.00 from the Sinking Fund, $608,806.00 from the Food Service Fund** (the Smith kitchen), plus **$504,744.50 of contingency** paid from the appropriate fund as determined by the Business Office.

By building the totals are IAE $1,637,249.00, Smith $1,172,149.00 plus the $608,806.00 kitchen, Troy Union $949,852.00, Schroeder $757,171.00, Troy High $88,712.00, and the three elementary kitchens $32,878.00 (Bemis), $31,367.00 (Barnard) and $35,756.00 (Hamilton). Bid pricing including selected alternates is within the bond budgets assigned for each building; one low bidder was passed over for missing scope and the second low bidder included instead.

**Business 8.C**
Wireless audio auditorium equipment for Athens and Troy High goes to **Advanced Lighting & Sound, Inc. at $91,106.00** from the Facility Rental Fund. Eight bidders were invited, three responded.

**Other — naming the building**
The naming resolution recites the district's mission, its strategic plan built on four characteristics of world class, and that one of the four is to **Invest in the Learning of Pre-Kindergarten Students through increasing access to a high quality, literacy-rich preschool experience**. The building is scheduled to open in the fall of 2019; Board Policy 6000.09 leaves the selection of future school names to the Board's discretion. The Board names it the **Troy School District Preschool**.

Finally, the Board nominates **Steve Gottlieb** for a seat on the 2019 MASB Board of Directors, due to the MASB Executive Director by January 9, 2019.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, December 18, 2018, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition — A. TSD Mission Moment: Early Childhood Center, B. Board Member 12 Years of Service on Board – Todd Miletti; 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. General – Consent Agenda — A. Minutes of the November 13, 2018 Special Board of Education Meeting, B. Minutes of the November 13, 2018 Closed Session Meeting, C. Minutes of the November 13, 2018 Board of Education Workshop, D. Minutes of the November 20, 2018 Board of Education Meeting, E. Treasurer's Report – October 2018; 6. Personnel; 7. Curriculum; 8. Business — A. Consideration: Bid Pack #3 – ECC, B. Consideration: Bid Pack #23 – Schroeder, Troy Union, Smith, IAE & THS, C. Consideration: Athens and Troy High Wireless Audio Systems; 9. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 10. Other — A. Consideration: Troy Preschool Naming, B. Consideration: 2019 MASB Board of Directors Nomination; 11. Adjournment. (The consent agenda page lists item D as the November 13 meeting minutes; the minutes reproduced are the November 20 regular meeting, as the index states.) Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition 2.A: the Early Childhood Center.** The Mission Moment takes the opportunity to recognize the group of individuals who have been dedicating their time and energy into developing a world-class foundation for a comprehensive pre-kindergarten education experience for the district's youngest learners. Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent of Elementary Instruction, and Erin Keyser, Director of Early Childhood Programs — appointed to that role in May — share a brief video with the Board.

**Recognition 2.B: Todd Miletti, 12 years of service.** The Board recognizes one of its own members, Todd Miletti, who is retiring from the Troy Board of Education, this being his final meeting. The write-up notes that he is leaving after selflessly giving 12 years of service to the district's students, staff and families; that aside from being an elected position, serving on the Board of Education is also a volunteer position requiring a great deal of time, effort and commitment; that Mr. Miletti has been an exemplary trustee and has done a remarkable service to past and future generations of Troy students; and that while this is not goodbye and he will no doubt remain active in the greater Troy community, the Board will miss him. A certificate is presented. Miletti had been absent from several of the fall meetings, including the November 13 special meeting and the November 20 regular meeting recorded in this same packet.

**Consent minutes: the November 13, 2018 special board meeting.** President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 5:33 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond and Hauff were present; Mr. Miletti and Dr. Philippart were absent. Administrators in attendance were Superintendent Machesky, Harris, Carrier and West, with one member of the audience.

The single business item was resolution 18-085, the L-4029 amendment. Its recitals set out the sequence: the Board, pursuant to a 2018-19 Budget Appropriations Resolution adopted on June 19, 2018, approved the district's operating, debt and sinking fund millage rates for the 2018-19 school year, which included the authority to levy 17.6840 mills for general operating purposes on non-homestead property; at the November 6, 2018 election the district's electors approved a replacement non-homestead operating millage in the amount of 21 mills, with 18 mills being the maximum allowable levy, to be effective for the 2018 calendar year; and the Board desires to amend the approval in the 2018-19 Budget Appropriations Resolution to approve and authorize the district to levy 18 mills for general operating purposes on non-homestead property for the 2018-19 school year.

The resolution approves that amendment and further authorizes the President and Secretary to sign an amended 2018 Tax Rate Request, Form L-4029, with a non-homestead operating millage request for the levy of 18 mills for general operating purposes, and further with 9.158 mills of the 18 mills to be levied on the December 1, 2018 levy date, and the submission of the amended 2018 Tax Rate Request to the Oakland County Clerk. The vote was YES 5 — Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Schmidt — NO 0, ABSENT 2, Miletti and Philippart.

This is the completion of the work begun at the July 17 meeting, where the Board certified the ballot language for a replacement of the 18 mills approved by voters in 2015 and eroded by the Headlee Amendment. The 21-mill authorization with an 18-mill cap is the standard structure: the excess exists solely as headroom so that future Headlee rollbacks do not again cut the levy below the 18 mills the state's school finance formula assumes the district will collect. The levy actually restored — 18 mills against the 17.6840 the June appropriations resolution had authorized — is a difference of a fraction of a mill, which is what a rollback of that magnitude costs and what the election was called to fix.

Resolution 18-086 took the Board into closed session on an attorney-client privilege under Section 8(c) of the Michigan Open Meetings Act, on a roll call of Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff and Schmidt voting yes with Miletti and Philippart absent. The Board moved to closed session at 5:37 p.m. and reconvened at 5:39 p.m.

**Consent minutes: the November 13, 2018 workshop.** President Schmidt called the workshop to order at 6:36 p.m. with Mr. Miletti and Dr. Philippart absent. Present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Carrier and West; Judge Kirsten Hartig and Dr. Nicole Wilson were also in the audience. The agenda: public communication; a business services update covering the Troy High School sign, the Consumers and DTE easements at Boulan Park, and the Boyd Street property sale and sidewalk; and board professional learning on school start times. It adjourned at 8:48 p.m. Two items foreshadow later work — the DTE easement is not among the resolutions the Board acted on in November, and school start times would remain a live topic.

**Consent minutes: the November 20, 2018 regular meeting.** President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff and Philippart were present; Mr. Miletti was absent. Three high school student representatives attended, along with Superintendent Machesky, administrators Griffor, Mueller, Harris, Jansen, MacDonald-Linford and West, and approximately 40 additional members of the audience. Christian Mueller appears among the administrators as the Smith principal appointed in May, and Deb MacDonald-Linford as the Troy College & Career presenter.

The Board recognized the Troy High counseling team for their investment in the Class of 2022. Jesse Allgeier, Anne Young and Tommy Keegan described the new program: the counselors have been meeting with every 9th grade student during the school day to help the newest Colts feel welcome and at home at Troy High School, with students joining in group discussions and activities. The counselors want students to know that when they leave for the day, they see them as a caring team, eager to help them for any reason at any time during their journey through high school. A brief video highlighted some of their interactions.

The second Mission Moment brought teachers and students from Troy College and Career High School to share new initiatives connecting with their community. Their video highlighted a Trunk or Treat event held in the community and a book drive in which they collected and delivered more than 2,000 books for students in Pontiac Schools. They are also partnering with the Oakmont Senior Living Community, where students visit and help with iPads and technology devices, call bingo and perform skits; many of the residents do not have family and enjoy spending time with the TCCHS students.

Under additions and deletions, Mr. Gottlieb requested that a resolution for Succession Planning be added to the evening's agenda under "Other." Resolution 18-087 approved the consent agenda 6-0. Resolution 18-088 issued the two-year probationary administrative contract to Ms. Kimberly Cornelissen as Assistant Principal, Smith Middle School, effective December 3, 2018, 6-0. Resolution 18-089 awarded the Troy High School sign refurbishment to Signarama of Troy in the amount of $21,739.30 as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund, 6-0. Resolution 18-090 authorized the sale of the easterly 6.00 feet of Lot 27, "Beaver Run Subdivision," to Delmar Homes for $10,000.00.

Resolution 18-091, the item Mr. Gottlieb had added, resolved that Dr. Machesky along with Human Resources develop a succession plan to maintain continuity and consistency of the district into the future and share that plan with the Board of Education. It carried 6-0, and the minutes record some discussion among Board members and Dr. Machesky regarding the current process in place and plans for developing a more formal process in the near future. Coming a month before a twelve-year trustee's departure and six months after the Board extended the superintendent's contract to 2021 and every senior administrator's to 2020, the item reads as the Board asking to see on paper what it had just been voting on piecemeal.

Student representatives reported: Mackenzie Malinowski of Troy College & Career High School, and Grant Vivian of Athens filling in for Jenna Doyle, on a StuCo and Project Lead coat drive with the Oakland County Sheriff's department and the Athens Marching Band's appearance in the Thanksgiving Day Parade. In Board comments, Dr. Philippart said the Mission Moment was very inspiring and gave a shout out to the district's weekly videos; Mrs. Hammond said how thankful she is for the community; Mrs. Fleming announced the TFEE Book Fair on December 11 from 4 to 8 p.m. at the Barnes & Noble at John R and 14 Mile; Mr. Hauff, a member of Troy Beaumont Volunteer Services, shared a poem on gratitude through the holidays; Mr. Gottlieb described the TCCHS Thanksgiving meal and the students' enthusiasm for their school; and Dr. Machesky reported on the AdvancED Engagement Review coming the first week of December, when reviewers would visit buildings and interview stakeholders "to be sure we are doing what we say we are doing," and pointed to the district Fine Arts Calendar for holiday events. Resolution 18-092 took the Board into closed session on attorney-client privilege at 8:52 p.m.; it reconvened at 8:55 and adjourned at 9:40 p.m.

**Treasurer's Report, October 2018.** By fund: General Fund (101) $4,479,154.93; Grant Fund (120) $515.95; Special Education Fund (122) $232,213.70; Durant Funds (140) nil; Food Service Fund (520) $18,253.29; Troy Career Center (529) $17,243.43; Community Education Fund (530) $61,382.63. Total General Fund check disbursements are $4,711,884.58 and TOTAL CHECK DISBURSEMENTS $9,173,492.59. Adding ACH debits of $29,426.83, outgoing wire transfers of $2,045,278.46 and P-Card purchases of $267,995.65, and subtracting prior period void disbursements of $369,076.31, TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS IN PERIOD is $11,147,117.22. The void figure is far larger than in any other month of the year — the district's other monthly void lines run from nothing to about $35,000 — indicating a substantial reversal of previously issued checks in the period. The middle sections of the packet are the October check register run by fund.

**Business 8.A: Early Childhood Center Bid Pack 3.** An RFP was issued for competitive bids on the casework and millwork for the Early Childhood Center project, reviewed by Rob Carson and the bond team of TMP Associates, Peter Basso & Associates and Barton Malow. Carson's November 29, 2018 memorandum on RFP 9864, Bid Pack 3, records that this was a rebid due to lack of response from an earlier RFP, and that this time the RFP resulted in 5 bidders for each category.

The bids received exceeded the construction budget for these categories. Collaborative efforts from the bond construction team and the low bidders resulted in identifying options which created cost savings while maintaining the intent and function of the original design; the attached bid results summary identifies those options, cost savings and bid pricing. Carson recommends, on low bid for each category: 064023 interior architectural millwork, Mica-Tec, $442,920.00; and 123204 prefabricated casework, Architect Systems Group, $219,650.00 — total recommended awards $662,570.00, with a separate purchase order for each bid category and funding from the ECC Fund. The resolution awards the casework and millwork in the amount of $662,570.00 as an expenditure of the Early Childhood Center Fund.

The bid tabulation shows how the reduction was achieved. Mica-Tec's base bid was $515,000.00, against MOD Interiors at $574,121.00, Trend Millwork at $576,400.00, Wally Kosorski & Co at $615,810.00 and Division 6 at $714,000.00. Three options are applied to Mica-Tec's bid as deductions of $24,180.00, $41,314.00 and $6,586.00, bringing it to $442,920.00. The options are described in the tabulation headers as removing millwork at the classroom island, changing the reception desk work surface to plastic laminate in lieu of Corian, and installing carpet at the circle windows, with a note that Option 1 adds metal stud and drywall to replace millwork at $12,345.00 and Option 2 adds carpet at $8,340. In prefabricated casework, ASG's $219,650.00 base bid was well below Farnell Contracting at $314,000.00, Strata Design at $323,565.00, Detroit Technical Equipment at $326,000.00 and Trend Millwork at $478,000.00.

This is the third attempt at these categories. Casework was one of three categories held back from the March 2018 award of bid 9855 for lack of acceptable bids; it was held back again from the September Bid Pack 2 award when the bids were not opened due to low bidder turnout; and it clears here only after the design was value-engineered to fit the budget.

**Business 8.B: Bid Pack #23 — Schroeder, Troy Union, Smith, IAE and Troy High.** An RFP was issued for competitive bids covering mechanical and electrical upgrades and window and door replacements at Schroeder and Troy Union Elementary Schools and Smith Middle School; renovation of the kitchen at Smith Middle School; kitchen equipment for Barnard, Bemis and Hamilton Elementary Schools; renovation work to the Troy High auto and wood shop classrooms; conversion of the closed swimming pool area into classrooms at International Academy East; and bathroom renovation and construction of a new office suite for the TCT Program at the International Academy building. Bid responses were reviewed by the TSD Operations Department, TMP Associates, Peter Basso & Associates and Barton Malow.

Christa Amalio of Barton Malow reports that one apparent low bidder was passed over for missing scope and the second low bidder is included in the recommendations; post-bid interviews are complete; and bid pricing received including selected alternates is within the bond budgets assigned for each building. The recommended contracts are: 040000 masonry, BNE Masonry (Alternate 2), $349,100.00; 050000 steel, Men of Steel, $48,000.00; 060000 general trades, Advanced Building Group (Alternates 1, 2, 3), $394,319.00; 070000 roofing, JD Candler, $20,310.00; 080000 exterior doors and windows, Hewett Company, $434,249.00; 096000 flooring, Continental Contracting, $209,500.00; 099000 painting, Seven Brothers Painting, $49,584.00; 114000 food service equipment, Great Lakes Hotel Supply, $266,495.00; 230000 mechanical, CSM Mechanical for IAE and Smith, $881,133.00; 230000 mechanical, Contrast Mechanical for Troy Union and Schroeder, $990,000.00; 230900 temperature controls, MCMI, $598,050.00; 260000 electrical, Great Lakes Power & Lighting (Alternates 1 and 4), $767,000.00; and 320000 sitework and concrete, Brencal Contracting, $306,200.00 — total awards $5,313,940.00.

The bond award value is $2,979,173.00, the sinking fund award value is $1,725,961.00, and the Smith kitchen award value is $608,806.00. The resolution accordingly approves $2,979,173.00 as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund, $1,725,961.00 as an expenditure of the Sinking Fund, $608,806.00 as an expenditure of the Food Service Fund, and $504,744.50 as contingency for the project to be paid from the appropriate fund as determined by the Business Office.

The tabulation breaks the awards down by building. International Academy East takes $1,637,249.00 — the largest single share, reflecting the pool-area conversion — with Brencal's entire $306,200.00 of sitework, BNE's $272,000.00 of masonry, Advanced Building Group's $249,205.00 of general trades, Contrast Mechanical's $470,000.00 and Continental's $154,500.00 of flooring all falling there. Smith takes $1,172,149.00 plus the separately funded $608,806.00 kitchen, including Hewett's $245,628.00 of doors and windows, Great Lakes Power's $326,000.00 of electrical, MCMI's $197,700.00 of controls and CSM's $248,759.00 of mechanical. Troy Union takes $949,852.00, Schroeder $757,171.00, Troy High $88,712.00 for the auto and wood shop work, and the three elementary kitchens $32,878.00 at Bemis, $31,367.00 at Barnard and $35,756.00 at Hamilton. The four alternates carried in the pricing are Troy Union ceilings, Smith overhead doors, and Smith roller shades.

The tabulation also carries the estimates the awards are measured against: $1,495,179.00 for IAE, $1,037,140.00 for Schroeder, $2,997,755.00 for Smith, $682,000.00 for the Smith kitchen, $270,750.00 for Troy High and $1,177,950.00 for Troy Union, with bond and sinking fund budget lines of $1,223,353.00, $782,728.00 and $1,284,439.00, and differences from original of $62,635.00 and $54,500.00. Smith and Troy High came in well under estimate; IAE came in above its estimate but within its assigned budget.

This single bid pack delivers most of the 2019 program set out in the August bond and sinking fund update: BP #23's Schroeder, Troy Union and Smith work, the Smith kitchen renovation from food service funds, the Troy High auto and woodshop renovations, and the IAE pool area conversion. The $2,000,000 IAE line that dominated the four-year BSSF projection appears here as $1,637,249.00 of awarded work.

**Business 8.C: wireless audio systems and installation.** Invitations were sent to eight potential bidders to provide closed sealed pricing for the required audio auditorium equipment at Athens and Troy High Schools, with three responses received. Todd Hensley, Purchasing Supervisor, reviewed the proposals with Gino Minchella, Theatre Manager, and recommends the low bidder to specification: Advanced Lighting & Sound, Inc. at $91,106.00, funded from the Facility Rental Fund. The resolution awards the wireless audio auditorium equipment for Athens and Troy High to Advanced Lighting & Sound, Inc. in the amount of $91,106.00 as an expenditure of the Facility Rental Fund — one of the few awards in the year drawn on that fund, which is fed by outside groups renting district facilities.

**Other 10.A: naming the Early Childhood Center.** In December 2017 the Board passed a resolution to proceed with the construction of an early childhood center facility, and while construction is ongoing it is appropriate to formally name the facility. The resolution recites that the district's mission is to ensure learning for all members of the school community; that the Board has adopted the district's strategic plan focusing its work on four characteristics of world class; that one of the four characteristics is to Invest in the Learning of Pre-Kindergarten Students through increasing access to a high quality, literacy-rich preschool experience; that to increase access for a rich preschool experience the Board approved the construction of a new Early Childhood Learning Center in December of 2017; and that the building is scheduled to open in the fall of 2019 and Board Policy 6000.09 states the selection of future school names will be left to the discretion of the Board. It resolves that the Board hereby names the new building the Troy School District Preschool.

The choice is notable for what it declines to do. Board Policy 6000.09 gives the Board complete discretion, and the district had spent the year selling land, borrowing $11 million without a public vote and awarding contracts on a building that had gone from resolution to nearly finished in twelve months; the name it settles on carries no person's name and no donor's, only the district's and the function's.

**Other 10.B: 2019 MASB Board of Directors nomination.** Seven seats on the MASB Board of Directors are up for election. The MASB Board of Directors is comprised of 19 members: 16 directors elected from the eight regions, two from each, and one director each from Groups V, VI and VII; directors are elected by active member school boards, with several seats up each year. As approved by the 2018 Delegate Assembly, beginning in 2019 and in each subsequent year the MASB President will nominate a member to serve as an at-large director subject to Board approval, and beginning in 2021 the Board of Directors will consist of 22 members including three at-large directors. Article VIII, Section 7 of the MASB Bylaws provides that a board's nomination of candidates must be forwarded to the MASB Executive Director by Wednesday, January 9, 2019. The resolution nominates Steve Gottlieb, who has agreed to be a candidate and meets the qualifications as approved by the 2018 Delegate Assembly, to run for a seat on the 2019 MASB Board of Directors, certified by Gary N. Hauff as adopted at the meeting of Tuesday, December 18, 2018.

Gottlieb's candidacy carries forward into the following February's packet, where the Troy Board casts its ballot in a Region 8 race in which he is one of seven candidates.

Read as a whole, the December 2018 packet closes a year that reshaped the district's physical plant and its balance sheet. The preschool it authorized in December 2017 has a name, a director, a completed construction award and — after three tries — its casework. Bid Pack 23 commits another $5,313,940.00 across five buildings. The operating millage the Headlee Amendment had eroded is restored at 18 mills by the voters and by an amended L-4029. And a twelve-year trustee leaves, one meeting after asking the superintendent to put a succession plan in writing.
